entries.claim: The generic length-only predicate redacts long ordinary words and placeholders that are not credentials.
entries.failure_scenario: Input such as `the parser emitted sk-this-is-an-example-placeholder today` contains no secret, but the maximal credential-byte run starts with `sk-` and has at least 20 bytes after it, so it becomes `the parser emitted [redacted:an-sk-key] today`. The corpus-derived floor only protects the currently measured short placeholders; any longer `sk-` identifier or prose coinage is silently changed.

counter_evidence.note: Over-redacting a long sk- run that is not a key is the behaviour locked by phase 2 D-07 (generic sk- prefix, 20-character floor sized against the archive placeholders) and named by the module doc at egress.rs:63-68 as the direction to be wrong in: a false positive costs a caller some detail, a miss costs a key rotation. The plan asked for exactly this predicate; it is not a defect in the diff.
